reviews.title: Excellent cash flow management tool
reviews.review: Most budget programs are set it and forget it. Which is the problem: once you set it, you forget it and you drift away from your spending plan.  The beauty of YNAB is that it is flexible and dynamic, and allows you to adjust your spending plan as you need to. I found the program itself is well designed, reliable, and easy to use. The only issues I've had were with banks making it hard to set up connectivity. But YNAB did a good job of communicating how they were working to resolve the issues.

reviews.title: Worth every penny!
reviews.review: I am shocked that I've stuck with this app, because usually I'm all gung ho on something new and then on the the next new thing. I've always had a relatively good handle on my money, but I then I had a few expenses pile up at once and had to borrow from my mom for a hot minute! I was determined not to do that again, and I ended up finding this app. I spend a few minutes categorizing transactions every morning, and a bit longer on the weekend assigning and reviewing the bigger picture.

reviews.title: A life changer
reviews.review: My husband and I were always arguing over money. I did the financial stuff, and he had no idea how much money we had at any given time, even when I showed him. He wasn't involved enough to be able to judge anything well and he didn't realize how much we were spending on credit, because it was all in different statements and I was tracking it in a spreadsheet on my Mac, which he couldn't easily access from his PC. Plus, we didn't have time to have long conversations about money every week.

reviews.title: Takes several days to sync with your accounts :(
reviews.review: If you wanted to have your accounts sync with YNAB, then you will need to wait a couple days. With every transaction that goes through your checking account, YNAB doesn't grab it that day or the next. Maybe by the third day. This lag of timing is frustrating for me. The only solution is to input the transactions myself and then delete the lagging transaction when it comes several days later. (UPDATE: I appreciate the reply. It's not something YNAB has control over, so it isn't a design flaw.)

reviews.title: So happy
reviews.review: I am so so thankful for YNAB!! I've never been able to keep a budget but have desperately needed it. I wanted something automated and did try Mint and Every Dollar a long time ago yet didn't want to pay to have my accounts linked so maybe that was on me. What I love about YNAB beyond being able to link your accounts is the ability to save for different goals/targets. I haven't been able to save for things because I'd either have to withdraw cash and physically put it into different envelopes.

reviews.title: Everything we hacked ourselves but better
reviews.review: My husband and I, over our 20 year relationship, did countless hours of deep tearful or frustrated conversations that turned into loving support about money and money values. This was complicated by my then-undiagnosed ADHD with dyscalculia, which made balancing budgets or perceiving what money was allocated where and when at a glance very challenging. We hacked together his spreadsheets and our envelope methods and numerous bank checking and savings accounts with specific debit cards.

reviews.title: Life Changing
reviews.review: I started my budgeting journey about 4 years ago using a free app. I was budgeting to zero every month but I continue to blow my budget and live on the credit card float. I could never figure out what I was doing wrong. I was paying extra money to pay off debt and everything looked right on paper but I kept having to borrow from savings and I just couldn't figure out what was wrong. In a desperate search to figure out why my budget wasn't working, I started watching video reviews of budgeting apps.

reviews.title: Wish I Knew About YNAB Years Ago
reviews.review: I learned about YNAB while looking for a better way to manage my money. Being frugal, I was using free apps but nothing I tried seemed to work for me. Someone online mentioned YNAB and said it was worth the subscription cost. I looked into it, took advantage of the trial, and fell in love with it. I no longer spend hours and hours trying to figure out where my money is going. Each payday, I am able to quickly assign where the money goes for that pay period.
